items.title: Navy Chooses Boeing to Build Next-Generation Jet Fighter
items.summary: The Navy chose  Boeing  to build its next-generation jet fighter, the latest in a run of contract wins at the aerospace giant’s military unit.  The deal, worth more than $20 billion, tasks Boeing with building the next-generation jets that will eventually replace the carrier-launched F/A-18 Super Hornet in the 2030s, the Navy said.  Boeing beat  Northrop Grumman  its only rival in the competition after  Lockheed Martin  dropped out of the running last year.

items.title: Boeing Wins Navy Contract for 6th Generation Fighter
items.summary: Tuesday, the Navy awarded Boeing a multi-billion-dollar contract to make its F/A-XX sixth-generation fighter jet.  Boeing stock rose $4.57, or 2.4%, in after-hours trading to $192.25.  “It’s an honor to be selected to produce the Navy’s first sixth–generation platform,” said Steve Parker, president and chief executive officer, Boeing Defense, Space & Security, in a news release.

items.title: Boeing wins $20 billion Navy award for next-generation fighter jet; shares rise
items.summary: Investing.com -- Boeing Co (NYSE:BA) shares advanced late Tuesday after the U.S. Navy selected the aerospace defense contractor to lead full-scale development of its next-generation carrier-based strike fighter.

items.title: Is GE Stock Riskier Than It Looks?
items.summary: GE Aerospace (GE) stock trades at an earnings multiple of 36.9, compared to 22.1 for the S&P 500. That's steep for a company like GE and needs justification. While management highlights that adjusted revenue has grown at least 20% in each of the last five quarters, that the high valuation assumes uninterrupted expansion. Yet in July, management acknowledged that demand is no longer the main driver of services growth. And that raises the question: Is GE Aerospace stock riskier than it looks.
